title: Review: living in Israel
why: Review of the "Living in Israel" unit: you compare the four binyanim you know and combine the hitpa'el, the hif'il, holidays and comparisons. It wraps up level A2, before the opinions and nuances of B1.

{"lessons": ["

Four binyanim, one system

You now know four binyanim. Each one has its own \"signature\" in the present, the past and the infinitive:

BinyanPresent (he)Past (he)Infinitive
pa'alכּוֹתֵב kotevכָּתַב katavלִכְתֹּב likhtov
pi'elמְדַבֵּר medaberדִּבֵּר diberלְדַבֵּר ledaber
hitpa'elמִתְלַבֵּשׁ mitlabeshהִתְלַבֵּשׁ hitlabeshלְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ lehitlabesh
hif'ilמַתְחִיל matkhilהִתְחִיל hitkhilלְהַתְחִיל lehatkhil

To recognize them in the present: מִתְ־ is the hitpa'el; מַ־ with a long i, the hif'il; מְ־ with a then e, the pi'el.

In the past, they all take the same endings (־תִּי, ־תָּ, ־נוּ, ־וּ…): only the beginning changes.

The meaning often follows the binyan: מִתְלַבֵּשׁ, to get dressed (yourself); מַלְבִּישׁ, to dress someone.

", "

Holidays and comparisons

Greetings: חַג שָׂמֵחַ for every holiday, שָׁנָה טוֹבָה on Rosh Hashanah, and to reply גַּם לְךָ / גַּם לָךְ.

Comparing: יוֹתֵר / פָּחוֹת + adjective + מִ־ (מֵ־ before א ה ח ע ר, מֵהַ־ before the article). The most: הֲכִי. The adjective always agrees.

בְּפֶסַח הַטִּיסוֹת יוֹתֵר יְקָרוֹת.At Passover, flights are more expensive. [be-pesakh ha-tisot yoter yekarot]
בַּבֹּקֶר אֲנִי מִתְאַרְגֵּן יוֹתֵר מַהֵר מִמָּאיָה.In the morning, I get ready faster than Maya. [ba-boker ani mit'argen yoter maher mi-Maya]
", "

Telling the story of a holiday

A short story in the past, with everything you've learned in this unit:

בְּפוּרִים שֶׁעָבַר הִזְמַנְתִּי חֲבֵרִים לִמְסִבָּה.Last Purim, I invited friends to a party. [be-purim she-avar hizmanti khaverim li-mesiba]
כֻּלָּם הִתְחַפְּשׂוּ, וְהַמּוּזִיקָה הִתְחִילָה בְּתֵשַׁע.Everyone dressed up, and the music started at nine. [kulam hitkhapsu, ve-ha-muzika hitkhila be-tesha]
זֶה הָיָה הָעֶרֶב הֲכִי טוֹב שֶׁל הַשָּׁנָה!It was the best evening of the year! [ze haya ha-erev hakhi tov shel ha-shana!]

To tell a story, link your sentences with אַחַר כָּךְ (then, afterward) and בַּסּוֹף (in the end): you've known them since the unit on the past.
